inputs.label: Special purpose deposit under today's rules
inputs.source: Set each year in capital planning; no figure is held, so it starts at zero

rules.quote: The highest priority use of Free Cash should be to increase the balance of the Stabilization Account if necessary to a level of at least five percent of the current fiscal year omnibus budget
The next highest priority use of Free Cash should be to fund an amount equivalent to at last 10% of the previous fiscal year’s certified General Fund Free Cash for deposit into the OPEB Trust Fund
The amount is to be calculated each fiscal year during the capital planning process
Any monies that remain in Free Cash may be used to fund one-time expenditures
The Town should maintain a balance in the general stabilization fund of no less than four percent of the prior year’s omnibus budget
The total of all funds should not exceed ten percent of the prior years’ omnibus budget

presets.label: State draft

rules.quote: Set aside at least 20 percent of the certified free cash amount as the starting balance for the next year’s free cash certification
Appropriate at least 1 0 percent to the special purpose stabilization funds
5 percent to the Town’s general stabilization
capped at 10 percent of the previous year’s total budget
Appropriate at least 10 percent to the Town’s other postemployment benefits (OPEB) trust fund
Apply at least 20 percent but no more than 30 percent to the cash capital budget
Apply at least 20 percent but no more than 30 percent to the cash capital budget
Use the lesser of 10 percent or $250,000 for noncapital special articles
with an annual appropriation of 0.3 percent of the current year general fund budget

presets.source: DLS draft financial policy manual, April 2024, pdf pages 28-30

presets.label: Custom
presets.source: Your own shares of the free cash

text.annual_note: The draft also sets a yearly stabilization deposit from the operating budget, not from free cash: 0.25% in its summary table, 0.3% in its text.
text.audit_note: The FY2025 audit prints the general stabilization balance as $3,237,894, not $3,147,179; the calculator starts from the figure the state's databank also prints.
text.budget_note: One budget figure is used wherever a rule names the current or the prior year's budget; edit it to test another year.
text.cap_reading: Our reading: today's "total of all funds" is taken as every stabilization fund, general and special purpose together.
text.floors_note: The draft's shares are floors ("at least"); the calculator applies each floor.

uses.label: Left for Town Meeting to decide

so.text: Under today's rules most of the free cash is left for Town Meeting to decide; under the draft most of it is assigned before Town Meeting sees it.
